body.text: uddiṣṭaṃ me āyuṣmantaḥ prātimokṣasūtroddeśasya nidānaṃ // uddiṣṭāś catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmās trayodaśa saṃghāvaśeṣā dharmā dvāv aniyatau dharmau | triṃśan naiḥsargikapāyantikā dharmāḥ navati pāyantikā dharmāś catvāraḥ pratideśanīyā dharmāḥ saṃbahulā śaikṣā dharmāḥ saptādhikaraṇaśamathā dharmā etāva

children.translated_text: is

children.text: tasya bhagavatas tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sūtragataṃ sūtraparyāpannam iti yo vā punar anyo 'py āgacched dharmasyānudharmaḥ tatra sahitaiḥ samagraiḥ saṃmodamānair avivadamānais tīvraś cetasa ārakṣāsmṛtyapramāde yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ // //
children.translated_text: contained in the <s>sūtra</s>s and included in the <s>sūtra</s>s of the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One; and whatever else may come that is in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> — therein, united, in harmony, rejoicing together, without quarreling, with zealous minds, effort should be made in the practice of vigilance, mindfulness, and non-negligence.

body.translated_text: I have recited for you, venerable ones, the introduction to the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> recitation. And there have been recited the four <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) rules, thirteen <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (suspension) rules, two <s>aniyata</s> (undetermined) rules, thirty <s>naiḥsargika pāyantikā</s> (forfeiture with confession) rules, ninety <s>pāyantikā</s> (confession) rules, four <s>pratideśanīya</s> (acknowledgment) rules, the numerous <s>śaikṣa</s> (training) rules, and the seven <s>adhikaraṇaśamatha</s> (methods for settling disputes) rules — this much

children.text: kṣāntiḥ paramaṃ tapas titikṣā nirvāṇaṃ paramaṃ vadanti buddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Patience is the supreme austerity, forbearance — the <s>Buddha</s>s declare <s>Nirvāṇa</s> to be supreme;

children.text: na hi pravrajitaḥ paropatāpī śramaṇo bhavati parān viheṭhayānaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: for one who has gone forth is not a tormentor of others; a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) does not harm others. //1//
As one with eyes [avoids] rough terrain, even when there is power to act,
so the wise person in this world of the living should avoid evil deeds. //2//

children.text: anopavādī nopaghātī prātimokṣe ca saṃvaraḥ {B: anupavādo 'nupaghātaḥ} /
children.translated_text: Not reviling, not harming, and restraint in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>;

children.text: mātrajñatā ca bhakte 'smin prāntaṃ ca śayanāsanam*
children.translated_text: and moderation in food, and secluded dwelling,
and devotion to the higher mind — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>s. //3//

children.text: yathāpi bhramaraḥ puṣpād varṇagandhāv aheṭhayan* [yathā hi] /
children.translated_text: Just as a bee [takes] from a flower color and fragrance without harming [it],

children.text: ḍayate rasam ādāya evaṃ grāme muniś caret* // 4
children.translated_text: and flies off having taken the nectar — so should a sage move through the village. //4//

children.text: na pareṣāṃ vilomāni na pareṣāṃ kṛtākṛtam* /
children.translated_text: Not [looking at] the faults of others, not [at] what others have done or not done;

children.text: ātmanas tu samīkṣeta samāni viṣamāṇi ca // 5
children.translated_text: but one should examine one's own [deeds], what is proper and what is improper. //5//

children.text: adhicetasi mā pramādyato munino maunapadeṣu śikṣataḥ {B:prāmodyato; maunipadeṣu} /
children.translated_text: Let not the sage be negligent regarding the higher mind, training in the path of silence;

children.text: śokā na bhavanti tāyina upaśāntasya sadā smṛtimataḥ // 6
children.translated_text: sorrows do not arise for one who is a protector, tranquil, and ever mindful. //6//

children.text: dadataḥ puṇyaṃ pravardhate vairaṃ saṃyamato na cīyate /
children.translated_text: For one who gives, merit increases; for one who restrains [himself], enmity does not accumulate;

children.text: kuśalī prajahāti pāpakaṃ kleśānāṃ kṣayatas tu nirvṛtiḥ {B: kṣayitas} // 7
children.translated_text: the skillful one abandons evil; through the destruction of the <s>kleśa</s>s (afflictions), there is <s>nirvṛti</s> (peace). //7//
The non-doing of all evil, the undertaking of what is wholesome,
the taming of one's own mind — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>s. //8//

children.text: kāyena saṃvaraḥ sādhu sādhu vācātha saṃvaraḥ {B: vācā ca} /
children.translated_text: Restraint by body is good, good is restraint by speech;

children.text: manasā saṃvaraḥ sādhu sādhu sarvatra saṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: restraint by mind is good, good is restraint in all things;
the <s>bhikṣu</s> restrained in all things is freed from all suffering. //9//

children.text: vācānurakṣī manasā susaṃvṛtaḥ kāyena caivākuśalaṃ na kuryāt* /
children.translated_text: Guarding one's speech, well-restrained in mind, and not doing unwholesome deeds with the body —

children.text: etāṃs trīn karmapathān viśodhya nārāgayen mārgam ṛṣipraveditam* // 10
children.translated_text: purifying these three courses of action, one should attain the path proclaimed by the sages. //10//

children.text: buddho vipaśyī ca śikhī ca viśvabhu krakutsundaḥ kanakamuniś ca kāśyapaḥ {B: krakutsandaḥ} /
children.translated_text: <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>, <s>Krakutsunda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s> — these <s>Buddha</s>s,

children.text: anuttaraḥ śākyamuniś ca gautamo devātidevo naradamyasārathiḥ // 11
children.translated_text: and the unsurpassed <s>Śākyamuni Gautama</s>, god above gods, the charioteer who tames men — //11//
of these seven heroic <s>Buddha</s>s, foremost leaders and protectors of the world,
this <s>Prātimokṣa</s> has been recited in full, of those glorious ones. //12//

children.text: asmin sagauravā buddhā buddhānāṃ śrāvakāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: In this [<s>Prātimokṣa</s>], the <s>Buddha</s>s showed reverence, and those who are disciples of the <s>Buddha</s>s;

children.text: asmin sagauravā bhūtvā prāpnumadhvam asaṃskṛtam* {B: prāptamadhvam} // 13
children.translated_text: having shown reverence in this, may you attain the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). //13//
Strive! Go forth! Exert yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ // 14
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant [crushes] a hut of reeds! //14//

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati /
children.translated_text: Whoever shall practice diligently in this <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>,
having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering. //15//
For the mutual protection of virtue and for the growth of the teaching,
this <s>Prātimokṣa</s> has been recited; the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance ceremony) has been performed by the <s>saṃgha</s>. //16//

children.text: yasyārthe sūtram uddiṣṭaṃ yasyārthe poṣadhaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whose sake the <s>sūtra</s> was recited, for whose sake the <s>poṣadha</s> was performed —

children.text: tac chīlam anurakṣadhvaṃ bālāgraṃ camaro yathā // 17
children.translated_text: guard that virtue, as a yak [guards] its tail-hair. //17//
Whatever merit has been accumulated from the recitation of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>,

children.text: aśeṣas tena loko 'yaṃ maunīndraṃ padam āpnuyāt // 18
children.translated_text: by that, may this entire world attain the state of the chief of sages (<s>Maunīndra</s>). //18//

body.text: /// prātimokṣaḥ samāptaḥ ///
body.translated_text: The <s>Prātimokṣa</s> is complete.
